units.source_text: 白居易自嘲诗：“五十八翁方有后，静思堪喜亦堪嗟。

en.t: Bai Juyi says in a poem mocking himself: At fifty-eight, this old man has only now had a child; thinking quietly on it, it is cause for joy and also for sighing.

units.source_text: 一珠甚少还惭蚌，八子虽多不羡鸦。

en.t: One pearl is very few, and I am still ashamed before the oyster; though a crow has eight young, I do not envy it.

units.source_text: 秋月晚生丹桂实，春风新长紫兰芽。

en.t: Under the autumn moon, the red cassia bears fruit late; in the spring wind, new shoots of purple orchid grow.

units.source_text: 持杯祝愿无他语，慎勿顽愚似汝爷！”

en.t: Raising my cup, I have no other blessing to give: take care not to be obstinate and foolish like your father!

units.source_text: 下文又引末句，“爷”指柏木也。

en.t: The following passage quotes the final line again; the word father refers to Kashiwagi.
